The papersThe code

Filtering, FDR and power, dug back up.

47 results: 6 exact, 7 agree, 22 partly agree, 8 inconclusive, 2 differ, 2 not attempted. The lost R scripts were rebuilt from the paper, the simulation and the leukemia analysis were run again, and every curve was laid over the authors' own vector figures.

Fig. 1

Fig. 1. P-value densities of the t test (8 df) under the null and the alternative, with no filter, the fold-change filter and the variance filter, 25% removed.

Partly agrees
Fig. 1, null hypothesis
100.0% within 2 px, Agrees
Fig. 1, alternative hypothesis
92.0% within 2 px, Partly agrees

The no-filter and fold-change curves match the published ones within 0.002 for p from 0.01 (0.004 below); the variance-filter curve does not: ours removes more small p-values (published 2.00 against ours 1.33 at p = 0.005; up to 0.71 apart, 0.54 for p from 0.01).

Fig. 6, the test's p-values above the boxes

With no noise term the box medians come back (0.50, 0.45, ..., 0.01 against 0.51, 0.46, ..., 0.01), but our quartiles sit about 3% low and the FDR lines are of another data set; the same boxes 5% larger score as well as ours. At x = 0 nothing is filtered and the test's p-value is uniform over data sets: the paper's 0.3 and our 0.6 both say 'no bias'. The ten '***' come back.

Every figure panel and claim of the paper and its Additional File 1. A figure panel agrees when 95% of the published ink lies within 2 px of ours and ours of it, at 300 dpi on the published panel's own axes, and no wrong or near-miss version scores as well.

Results: childhood leukemia (Figs 7 and S5)Partly agrees3 of 4 values
  • signal and variance: achieved FDR stays around 5% (mean over x = 0 to 0.8 within 0.025 of 0.05, every size): paper yes, ours no
  • fold change: achieved FDR rises with x (x = 0.8 above x = 0 by 0.05 or more, every size): paper yes, ours yes
  • power rises with sample size (8 < 16 < 24 at x = 0): paper yes, ours yes
  • fold change raises power; signal and variance have no or the opposite effect (gain below 0.02; x = 0.5 against 0, every size): paper yes, ours yes
On our subset of 24 per group the signal and variance filters' achieved FDR averages about 0.10, not about 5%: the subset is one random draw (the paper's figure satisfies the rule).

R package filterfdr and its tutorialAgrees

The main finding holds: the fold-change filter biases the FDR and raises power, and the signal and variance filters do not bias it. Three sentences overstate the paper's own figures, and Fig. 3's caption swaps two curves; the power gaps of Figs 5, S2, S5 and S6 are open.

What came back

Fig. 4
Achieved FDR for four methods within 0.004 at every point but one.
Fig. 3
pi0 for every filter within 0.004, once the caption's swapped labels are put back.
Fig. 1
The null densities exactly, and two of the three alternative curves.
Fig. 6
The test's box medians, from data without the noise term.
The method
Simulation, filters, FDR-bias test and p-value densities as the R package filterfdr.

What stayed buried

  • The authors' R scripts: the paper's link and its zip are gone.
  • Seeds, the subsets drawn from the leukemia data, and the settings of bootFDR and permFDR (Figure S7).
  • Why the paper's power is a little higher than ours in Figs 5, S2, S5 and S6: tested causes ruled out.

The main finding holds: the fold-change filter biases the FDR and raises power, and the signal and variance filters do not bias it. Three sentences overstate the paper's own figures, and Fig. 3's caption swaps two curves; the power gaps of Figs 5, S2, S5 and S6 are open.

What we matched

How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.

Simulation
5000 features, 10 per group, pi0 0.8, bitriangular effects as in the first author's SSPA; noise SD 0.1 per feature.
Filters
Signal, fold change and variance, cut at their empirical quantiles.
Corrections
BH, BY, multtest's two-stage aBH and qvalue, at 5% and at 21 levels.
Bias test
Rows permuted one by one, BH-based KS per permutation, then a one-sided KS over 1000 permutations.
Leukemia
GSE13425, 44 TEL-AML1 against 44 hyperdiploid, limma, truth from all 88.

Filtering, FDR and power came back from the paper's text and its vector figures; the scripts did not.
